title: The Single Expression

canonical_node.axiom: Creation is one act expressed four ways: time, space, matter, motion; no member is prior.
definitions: Vestigium Trinitatis: trace of the Trinity in creation
derivation: Sheet 000 established the Fullness as one being in three persons.
Creation begins when the Fullness speaks outward.
The first act cannot be an assembly; it must be an expression.
Genesis 1:1-2 presents time, space, matter, and motion in one verb (bara) without sequence.
Attempting to order the four leads to contradictions: matter needs space, space needs matter, motion needs space and time, time needs change.
Therefore, the four are not sequential but simultaneous aspects of one act.
This structure mirrors the perichoretic shape of the Trinity, a vestigium Trinitatis.
canonical_node.action: Treat time, space, matter, and motion as co-original aspects of a single creative act, not as separable entities with priority.
boundary: Does not claim to prove the Trinity from physics.
Does not assert that the unorderability result holds under Newtonian absolute space.
Does not provide a full derivation of the cosmos from first principles.
test: Check that any proposed ordering of the four fundamentals leads to a contradiction.
Verify that the relational view of space is assumed; if absolute space is used, the unorderability result may fail.
Confirm that the vestigium claim is treated as correspondence, not proof.

dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a unified framework for the four fundamentals as one act, enabling a non-sequential ontology.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the Trinity as ground; creation is not derived from physics.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: Without this node, the four fundamentals remain separate and ordered, losing the perichoretic signature and the basis for the vestigium claim.

classification.recommended_atom_action: preserve as working sheet; flag as not proven

overstatement_risks: Claiming the unorderability result is proven when it depends on relational space.
Elevating the vestigium to a proof of the Trinity.
Conflating the four faces in creation with the four debts in God.
kill_conditions: If absolute space is shown to be viable, the unorderability argument fails.
If the perichoretic structure is not uniquely Trinitarian, the vestigium claim weakens.
risk.lean_target: A formalization of the unorderability argument under relational space, and a clear statement of the vestigium as abductive.

plain_summary: This sheet argues that creation is a single act with four inseparable aspects: time, space, matter, and motion. It claims these cannot be ordered without contradiction, and that this structure mirrors the Trinity, serving as a trace (vestigium) but not a proof. The argument relies on a relational view of space and is not a formal proof.
